name: Tata Chemicals Ltd
title: Tata Chemicals Ltd - 500770 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Soda ash oversupply persists with China inventory near 1.89 Mt and export pressure; consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 381 cr from 537 cr on UK gas costs and Kenya suspension, with no capacity cut from Tata Chemicals.

summary.headline: Tata Chemicals Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR381 crore (from INR537 crore) and the company posted a loss after tax of INR50 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR1,303 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to INR292 crore, but standalone PAT fell 31% to INR122 crore. Consolidated results were hit by UK gas and energy cost spikes, lower overseas realisations (US exports to Southeast Asia), logistics costs, and the suspension of Kenya operations. Management described soda ash markets as oversupplied, with prices expected to stay range-bound. Net debt excluding leases stood at INR6,127 crore.

segments.name: Living Essentials (bicarbonate, salt, FOS)
segments.commentary: Standalone India volumes rose on salt, FOS and silica. The UK salt and bicarbonate operations drove the consolidated EBIT loss, from gas and energy costs and higher cost of feedstock soda ash for bicarbonate. Management expects these costs to normalise as energy and logistics costs moderate.

segments.name: Industrial Essentials (soda ash, silica)
segments.commentary: Global soda ash is oversupplied, with China as the key driver. Indian domestic prices softened late in the year, and US export pricing remains under pressure. DGTR has recommended two years of import quantity restrictions after imports rose 89% in FY2024.

segments.name: US (TCNA)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose on volumes from contracts acquired during the year, partly offset by lower export pricing. The company won Searles Valley Minerals Chapter 11 contracts covering half a million tonnes over two years. The US$22 million payment is being amortised as an intangible over five years.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on lower salt realisation. Variable costs rose sharply on gas prices, and this was the main drag on consolidated EBIT.

segments.name: Kenya
segments.commentary: Operations have been suspended since a Ministry of Mining notice. Management says the operation is debt-free and was margin positive. The company is pursuing legal and administrative routes, and a court hearing is expected in November.

segments.name: Farm Essentials (Rallis)
segments.commentary: Monsoon shortfall and delayed sowing hurt agrochemical demand early in the period, but Kharif acreage recovered. Rallis delivered resilient performance, aided by crop care and soil health, while profitability was pressured by input cost inflation.

guidance_outlook: Near-term soda ash market expected to remain range-bound due to Chinese capacity additions and sustained export activity.
Pricing is expected to stay range-bound; sustained improvement depends on supply rationalisation and demand growth in applications and geographies.
Capex of around INR1,000 crore for the current year, including growth projects; next year expected to be roughly the same.
UK energy and logistics costs expected to moderate and return to normal levels.
Focus on cost competitiveness, supply chain resilience, working capital optimisation, debt reduction and disciplined capital allocation.
capex_capacity: Capex of around INR1,000 crore for FY27, including growth projects; FY28 expected at a similar level.
Kenya: the company had been in the midst of doubling capacity and adding a bicarbonate unit, plus seeking a partner for container glass. These plans are now affected by the suspension.
Searles Valley contracts add about half a million tonnes to be served over two years, benefiting from proximity to California and Mexico markets.
Inner Mongolia Berun's 5 million tonne phase one had maintenance outages in October, expected to return to full rates at month end (Chinese supply side).
demand_pricing: Global soda ash: persistent oversupply, weak Chinese real estate and construction demand, and high Chinese export volumes. Chinese producer inventory reached about 1.89 million tonnes by end-September.
India: demand growth remains healthy, supported by solar glass capacity and infrastructure. Imports rose 89% in FY2024 and remain elevated.
Southeast Asia exports are unremunerative; the company is serving only residual contracts and will focus on the Americas and positive-netback markets.
Farm Essentials: uneven rainfall and delayed sowing hit parts of the quarter. Cautious agricultural outlook with weather, crop prices and input costs as near-term risks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Kenya operations and the possible course of action?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations remain suspended after a Ministry of Mining notice. The company is pursuing administrative engagement and a legal route, citing the UK-Kenya BIT and a lease running to 2053. The Environment and Land Court is due to hear the matter in November. Management would not give a timeline for restart.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the UK-related EBIT loss in Living Essentials, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is mainly UK salt and bicarbonate, due to higher gas and energy costs and higher feedstock soda ash logistics cost for bicarbonate. Q2 saw a sharp spike and these costs are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What contribution margins and accounting apply to the Searles Valley contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: The $22 million paid is recorded as an intangible and amortised over five years. Pricing is substantially above the export option, though exact figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will other US producers' shutdowns force the company to cut capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Southeast Asia exports are unremunerative and it is serving only residual contracts. Strategy is unchanged and it will focus on the Americas and positive-netback markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR796 crore proceeds from sale of non-current investments, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The proceeds came from selling listed shares in group companies in July, used to repay US and UK debt. The company holds about INR8,000 crore of group company shares at market value. Capex is about INR1,000 crore this year and similar next year, including growth projects.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company monetise its Tata Sons stake to reward shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on this.

risks_watch: Kenya suspension: outcome of the November court hearing, and the risk of losing the business or compensation through treaty arbitration.
Soda ash oversupply: Chinese export volumes, producer inventory of about 1.89 million tonnes, and possible further US capacity cuts.
UK gas and energy costs and Middle East freight volatility affecting consolidated margins.
Consolidated PAT before exceptional items and NCI was only INR10 crore in H1 FY27, against INR535 crore a year earlier.
Monitor whether Indian soda ash import quantity restrictions are imposed following the DGTR recommendation.
Net debt of INR6,127 crore excluding leases; progress on debt reduction through group stake sales.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious. Management openly described the soda ash market as oversupplied and the operating environment as challenging, and was measured on Kenya, saying it is pursuing legal routes with no timeline. It was confident on India volumes and on the Searles contracts, and declined to comment on the Tata Sons stake question.
key_quotes: Despite a resilient operating standalone performance, our consolidated results were sharply impacted by natural gas cost increases in U.K.
Market conditions are characterized by persistent oversupply, subdued industrial demand, especially in China, and intense competition across export markets.
We remain committed to Kenya, we remain committed to the business, and we will do whatever is right the way we run our businesses in a very ethical and sustainable manner.

adds.what: Searles Valley Minerals Chapter 11 contracts, ~0.5 million tonnes to be served over two years (contracts won, not owned capacity)

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects soda ash prices to stay range-bound amid oversupply, with capex of about INR1,000 crore in FY27 and similar in FY28 (a cut from ~INR1,200 crore), and no new owned capacity added beyond the Searles contracts, while Kenya expansion is suspended.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA fell to INR381 crore from INR537 crore YoY, but management expects UK gas and energy and logistics costs to normalise, while soda ash pricing stays range-bound, so the rebound is conditional.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new owned capacity beyond the Searles contracts (~0.5 million tonnes over two years, contracts not owned plants); Kenya capacity doubling and bicarbonate unit are suspended, and capex is about INR1,000 crore in FY27 with a similar FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR1,303 crore with India volumes up on salt, FOS and silica, and Searles adds volume, though Southeast Asia exports are being cut to residual contracts.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is being held at about INR1,000 crore in FY27 and a similar level in FY28, down from about INR1,200 crore, with no new plant announced and debt reduction as the stated priority.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was given, and soda ash pricing is expected to stay range-bound amid oversupply, with Chinese inventory at about 1.89 million tonnes.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consolidated PAT before exceptional items and NCI was INR10 crore in H1 FY27 versus INR535 crore a year earlier, and the Kenya suspension and UK cost drag remain open risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or brand launch was discussed on the call.

rows.label: DGTR import quantity restrictions on soda ash
rows.why: DGTR recommended two years of import quantity restrictions after imports rose 89% in FY2024, but the final imposition is not confirmed.

rows.label: Kenya operations restart or legal resolution
rows.why: Operations are suspended and a Environment and Land Court hearing is due in November, but management gave no restart timeline and treaty arbitration is an alternative route.

rows.label: Debt reduction via group stake sales
rows.why: INR796 crore of listed group shares were sold in July to repay US and UK debt, and about INR8,000 crore of group shares remain at market value against net debt of INR6,127 crore.

tone.note: Management was cautious on soda ash oversupply, range-bound pricing and the Kenya suspension with no restart timeline, and confident on India volumes and the Searles contracts; analysts pushed on the UK cost drag, Kenya and the Tata Sons stake, which management declined to address.
